coding.description: Read workspace files (model.py, tasks, reports, or authored Blender scripts), selected candidate artifacts, or public SDK docs/examples. SDK implementation source is unavailable. Use offset/limit for a 1-based line window.
coding.name: read_file

coding.description: Read deterministic gate evidence with identity validation. Unlike read_file, this returns FRESH or STALE for motion evidence and/or the exact candidate physics report.
coding.name: read_gate_evidence

coding.description: Overwrite an entire file. Default target is model.py (the SDK source of truth). Pass `path` = blender/<name>.py to author a headless-Blender bpy script (for run_blender) when you need organic/freeform geometry the CAD SDK cannot express. Pass `path` = tasks.json to author the downstream manipulation-task spec (see the Manipulation tasks section of your system prompt); it does not affect the compile gate.
coding.name: write_file

coding.description: Apply one or more exact-string edits to a file in a SINGLE call (default model.py; pass `path`=blender/<name>.py to edit a Blender script). `edits` is an ordered list of {old_str, new_str, replace_all?}: by default each old_str must occur EXACTLY ONCE. Set `replace_all` to true only when every occurrence should change. Ambiguous edits report every line/column. ATOMIC — if any edit is invalid or missing, NOTHING is written. Successful calls return a bounded unified diff. BATCH all of this turn's changes into one call instead of many single-edit calls.
coding.name: replace

coding.description: Build organic/freeform geometry (soft cushions, upholstery, molded shells — shapes the CAD SDK cannot express) by running a headless-Blender bpy script you authored at blender/<name>.py (via write_file). The script must build a single watertight MESH object and call export_result(obj); `bpy`, `bmesh`, `mathutils` are in scope. The driver decimates to a triangle budget and stages inputs/<out_name>.obj — attach it as ONE OF A PART'S VISUALS via mesh_from_input('<out_name>') (it can coexist with primitive visuals on the same part). If THIS script owns interfaces later consumed by placement, pass placement-relevant semantic Anchors through export_result(obj, anchors=[...]) and resolve them with semantic_anchor; decorative Meshes need none. Geometry only; set color via the SDK Visual. Returns the mesh report (tris/watertight/components/aabb/dims/anchor_count) so you can verify geometry and placement metadata.
coding.name: run_blender

coding.description: Search the SDK example corpus. Optionally filter by joint_type (revolute|prismatic|continuous|fixed).
coding.name: find_examples

coding.description: Keyword-search the INSTALLED CadQuery API only, so signatures are version-exact. Use this for CadQuery methods/selectors/classes on the public API surface, e.g. lookup_cadquery_api("revolve"), lookup_cadquery_api("slot2D"), lookup_cadquery_api("max Z face"), lookup_cadquery_api("bevel corner"). It returns the few matches most likely to fit your intent: qualified name, signature, and one-line doc. Do NOT use it for Artisan SDK helpers/classes such as MotionLimits, TestContext, mesh_from_cadquery, Material, Part, or Articulation; read model_contract.md or the SDK docs for those. Pass full=true to read ONE entry's complete docstring + signature; pass klass to scope the search to a CadQuery class available in the installed package, such as Workplane, Solid, Sketch, or selectors.
coding.name: lookup_cadquery_api

coding.description: Keyword-search the INSTALLED Blender bpy API (operators + bmesh.ops + modifier types) so names/args are version-exact — use it BEFORE writing a blender/<name>.py script, e.g. lookup_blender_api("solidify thickness"), lookup_blender_api("decimate"), lookup_blender_api("subsurf levels"), lookup_blender_api("displace texture"), lookup_blender_api("bmesh bridge loops"). Returns the few most relevant matches: qualified name, signature/args, one-line description. Pass full=true to read ONE entry's complete doc + arg list. For Blender authoring only — use lookup_cadquery_api for CadQuery and read_file/model_contract.md for the SDK model API.
coding.name: lookup_blender_api

coding.description: Inspect the current model.py geometry WITHOUT the pass/fail gate. Call with NO args to get the bare structure (parts, joints, axes, limits). Pass `code` (a short Python snippet ending in exactly one `emit(value)`) to MEASURE geometry: helpers injected into scope include part(name)/visual(...), aabb(obj)/dims(obj)/center(obj), pair_report(a,b)/overlap_report(a,b)/mount_report(child,parent), find_clearance_risks(...), geometry_connectivity_report(part). Use this to ROOT-CAUSE an overlap/size/floating issue — e.g. `emit(overlap_report(part('a'), part('b')))` or `emit(dims(part('lamp_head')))` — before repositioning geometry.
coding.name: probe_model

coding.description: RENDER your current model.py so you can SEE it (you otherwise only have probe numbers — rendering closes that blind spot for wrong shape/identity, wrong world orientation (lying vs standing), or a floating/penetrating part). `views` are named presets (front/side/top/perspective, each optionally with an `_open` or `_closed` suffix — `_open` drives every moving joint to its limit at once); `focus=[part_or_joint,...]` aims the camera at and zooms into the named parts/joints (use the real names from probe_model). The image comes back AS THIS TOOL'S RESULT — exactly like probe_model/compile output, with no extra delay — so look at it when you next act (don't say you've seen it in the same turn you call it). Use it to VERIFY a suspected visual/spatial fault before AND after an edit; prefer ONE targeted batch over many calls, and still use probe_model for exact dims/overlap numbers. `segment`=true recolours each PART a distinct flat colour (a 'semantic map') so a part buried inside another reads as a foreign colour the dark faithful materials hide — use it to confirm a suspected penetration / that two parts only touch where they should.
coding.name: request_render

coding.description: Compile model.py through Artisan (URDF export + schema validate + FCL rest-pose overlap + isolated-part / scale QC + run_tests). Call before finishing. For complete blocker or placement evidence, use read_file('reports/compile_findings.json'); for complete candidate-warning strings, use read_file('reports/physics_validation.json'). Treat either report as current only when its model_sha256 matches the current model.py.
coding.name: compile_model

coding.description: File a short structured note FOR THE REVIEWAGENT: what you changed this round, which overlaps/contacts/choices are intentional-by-design (with the reason), and any incoming issue you believe is a false positive (with your reasoning). Call this ONLY when the harness asks (a <handoff_ready> prompt after the motion self-check passes) — filing it hands off to the ReviewAgent. Do NOT file it during repair iterations.
coding.name: record_handoff_note

design.description: Submit the completed intake JSON. It is validated and stored as the blueprint asset_brief before engineering authoring begins.
design.name: submit_intake

design.description: Submit the complete engineering blueprint JSON (the filled template). It is validated immediately; on failure you get the errors and must fix and resubmit. A valid submission proceeds to self-review.
design.name: write_blueprint

design.description: Submit the agent-led review of the current blueprint. PASS releases P1; REDO requires a complete revised blueprint in this conversation.
design.name: submit_blueprint_selfcheck

review.description: Read model.py (ground every claim in the real source), qa_tests.py, the blueprint, the CodingAgent's tasks.json (the downstream manipulation spec — verify its bindings), selected candidate artifacts, or public SDK docs/examples. Reads are restricted to the workspace, selected artifacts, and public references; SDK implementation source is unavailable. Use offset/limit for a 1-based line window.
review.name: read_file

review.description: Read deterministic gate evidence with identity validation. Returns FRESH or STALE independently for motion evidence and exact candidate physics.
review.name: read_gate_evidence

review.description: Inspect the model WITHOUT a pass/fail gate. NO args → the STRUCTURE (real part/joint names + axes/limits, so `target`/`code_ref` are exact). Pass `code` (a short Python snippet ending in exactly one `emit(value)`) to MEASURE geometry and verify a render suspicion — helpers in scope include part(name)/visual(...), aabb/dims/center, pair_report(a,b)/overlap_report(a,b)/mount_report(child,parent)/geometry_connectivity_report(...) (signatures: read_file("probe_tooling")). Prefer this over authoring a throwaway qa_test just to read one number.
review.name: probe_model

review.description: Write the WHOLE qa_tests.py (one `def qa_tests(ctx):`). Use this for the FIRST version or a full rewrite; for small round-to-round changes prefer edit_test. The file persists across rounds (goalpost stability).
review.name: write_test

review.description: Incrementally edit qa_tests.py: replace the first exact occurrence of old_str with new_str (like a surgical patch). Prefer this over rewriting the whole file when adding/adjusting one assertion.
review.name: edit_test

review.description: Run the current qa_tests.py against the model. Returns {ok, failures:[{name,details}], error}.
review.name: run_tests

review.description: Render the build; the image comes back as this tool's result, visible when you next act (same as any tool's output, no extra delay). `views`: named presets (front/side/top/perspective, optional _open/_closed). `pose`: joint->value to drive a specific configuration (motion sweep). `camera`: a free angle {azimuth_deg,elevation_deg,distance_mult}. `focus`: part/joint name(s) to AIM the camera at and ZOOM into (a joint = a tight close-up on its pivot); combine with views/camera for a clean line of sight — a PAID render, so use crop_region for a free zoom of an existing image first. `segment`=true recolours each PART a distinct flat colour (a 'semantic map') so a part buried inside another reads as a foreign colour the dark realism materials hide — use it to verify any overlap/declared contact.
review.name: request_render

camera.description: Free camera angle: azimuth_deg + elevation_deg orbit the object; distance_mult scales framing distance (>1 pulls back, <1 zooms in). Omit for the default view.

pose.description: Joint name -> position map (free-form), e.g. {'input_shaft_spin': 0.785}, to drive a specific configuration for a motion-sweep render. Radians for revolute/continuous, metres for prismatic. Omit (or {}) for the rest pose. Pose the DRIVER of a coupled mechanism; the follower tracks it automatically.

review.description: Zoom a sub-region of a rendered image to inspect a small/contact feature (hinge seam, latch, rim). Coordinates are NORMALIZED 0..1 with the ORIGIN at the TOP-LEFT, where 0.5 is the center; coarse is fine.
review.name: crop_region

image.description: Name of the rendered image to crop (e.g. 'perspective_open.png').

review.description: Finish the review with the structured verdict. Provide overall realism_rating (0-10), rubric scores for THIS phase's dimensions (0-10 each; you'll be told which — score others only if you gathered evidence, never a guess), a summary, and the issues you found. You do NOT state a proceed/revise decision: it is DERIVED from your scores + issue severities (a blocking issue, or any gating dim < 5, routes a redo). Complete every required evidence step before submitting.
review.name: submit_review
